Board members discussed retroactive term alignments for transportation board appointees [1:37:33, 1:41:12] and approved an appointment to the Small Business Advisory Committee [5:31:47]. The meeting included public hearings on proposed town meeting warrant articles, including Article 1 regarding policy violations and legislative immunity [2:26:52, 2:27:26], Articles 15 and 16 concerning zoning changes and a Memorandum of Agreement for 26 Pleasant Street [3:09:26, 4:43:23, 4:48:54], a presentation on commercial rezoning process recommendations [5:33:14, 5:35:19], and Article 20 regarding traffic enforcement and Vision Zero goals [6:06:21, 6:10:15].

Todd of Nordblum Company presented the development plan for 26 Pleasant Street [4:25:23], while co-sponsor Linda Pelky and other residents spoke on neighborhood impacts [3:19:06, 3:44:55]. Staff member Meredith and consultant Emily Andis presented the commercial area process review [5:31:14, 5:33:14, 5:35:19]. Residents can also follow further updates on the commercial rezoning engagement framework [5:44:00, 6:05:35] and final petition adjustments to Warrant Article 20 heading into Town Meeting [6:07:33, 6:15:21].

summary: The board convened in executive session regarding an investigation [23:08] before returning to the public meeting [1:26:52] to approve omnibus items 6B through 6I [1:32:26] and discuss staggering term expirations for local board vacancies [1:37:39]. The board interviewed candidates and voted on appointments to the Board of Library Trustees [1:48:11] and reviewed updates to employee pay and classification structures following labor negotiations [2:16:39]. David Leuier presented a warrant article addressing town meeting member legislative immunity and complaint investigation procedures [2:23:39]. The board then held a lengthy hearing on Warrant Article 15 concerning a zoning overlay development project at 26 Pleasant Street, receiving public testimony regarding heat island concerns, tree canopy preservation, traffic, and affordable housing [3:09:11], while reviewing a modified memorandum of agreement presented by town staff [4:44:02]. Afterwards, consultant Emily Keys Innes presented findings and recommendations to improve future commercial planning and public engagement processes [5:35:13], and the board reviewed a warrant article resolution regarding traffic enforcement and police funding allocation [6:06:09].
